claims.rationale: Cross-species biodistribution literature and characterization guidance indicate limited translatability absent orthogonal intact-EV analytics and controlled bridging studies.
claims.statement: Rodent intranasal biodistribution data alone are insufficient to predict reproducible intact-EV CNS exposure in larger species without matching intact-EV assays and bridging controls.

claims.rationale: No MCB/WCB, validated scale-up or reproducibility data provided; MISEV recommends defined production controls and reporting.
claims.statement: Current materials do not demonstrate characterized source-cell MCB/WCB or scalable, reproducible production sufficient to support advancing a specific intranasal formulation.

claims.rationale: MISEV2023 consensus supports orthogonal characterization and transparent release/assay criteria to de-risk identity and potency claims.
claims.statement: An orthogonal QC panel (particles, protein, lipid markers per MISEV), validated intact-EV assays (LLOQ, specificity, precision), and stability-indicating, mechanism-linked potency assays are required before formulation advancement.

evidence.excerpt: Curated summary: the ISEV consensus identifies continuing challenges in EV nomenclature, separation from non-vesicular particles, characterization, functional studies, production reporting, and in-vivo evaluation; it recommends transparent, orthogonal characterization and appropriate controls.
evidence.title: Minimal information for studies of extracellular vesicles (MISEV2023): From basic to advanced approaches

hypothesis.rationale: To ensure observed in vivo signal is attributable to intact EV and is reproducible across lots/species, the program must meet orthogonal analytical and process reproducibility criteria before bridging studies.
hypothesis.statement: Advancing an intranasal formulation into high-confidence delivery and cross-species PK/PD testing requires completion of a defined CMC/analytics/formulation compatibility gating package.
hypothesis.test_plan: Stage 1 completion criteria: MCB/WCB produced; orthogonal QC panel defined and assays fit-for-purpose validated (LLOQ, specificity, precision); stability-indicating potency assay correlated to an in vivo PD endpoint; reproducible release/stability/potency across ≥3 GMP-like batches; formulation/device compatibility with intact-EV recovery demonstrated ex vivo and in vivo (controls included).

matter.question: What evidence-linked identity and potency framework is needed before comparing SGL-001 lots or formulations?
matter.title: Potency and identity characterization
matter.why_it_matters: Without reproducible identity and potency measures, observed biological differences may reflect uncontrolled product variability.

program.current_formulation_hypothesis: Intranasal mesenchymal-stromal-cell-derived small-EV preparation with defined identity, purity, dose, and a mechanism-relevant potency assay; therapeutic cargo remains to be selected.
program.largest_unresolved_risk: Intranasal CNS exposure observed in rodents may not translate to larger species or humans.
program.name: SGL-001 development program
program.next_proposed_action: Program lead to assemble Stage-1 package (GLP large-animal intranasal biodistribution/tox, three GMP-like scale-up runs with draft specs and stability, validated potency/orthogonal QC plan, and regulator briefing) and request pre-IND/Scientific Advice in two jurisdictions; 3-month timeline.

risks.description: Lack of MCB/WCB, orthogonal QC, validated potency/stability assays, and scale-up reproducibility may produce misleading in vitro and in vivo results and block regulatory acceptance.
risks.mitigation: Execute Stage 1 actions: generate MCB/WCB, define/validate orthogonal assays, produce representative GMP-like batches, and document stability/potency reproducibility. Escalate assay development resourcing if timelines slip.
risks.title: Insufficient CMC/analytics to establish intact-EV identity, potency, and lot-to-lot reproducibility
